title: The move verb: the holder checkpoints and releases, and the item is reserved for its target

story.as_a: session, coordinating session or Mark in fleet_dash
story.i_want_to: say 'move this item to x1' (or to a session, or to the loop) and have the current holder checkpoint, release, and the item wait for that target alone
story.so_that: moving between machines and between sessions is one operation with one record, replacing the prose handoff

rationale: PRD R3: 'Moving is one verb ... the current holder checkpoints (R1) and releases, and the target pulls.' Today the only ways to hand an item on are a release that sends it to the queue for anyone (Stages.follow_release/5, lib/loopctl/delivery/stages.ex:1731, counted as an attempt unless the cause says otherwise, :179) or a handoff post nobody is bound to. Neither names a target, keeps the item away from other claimants, nor ships the holder's state. This story refactors the release path with a :moved edge and cause and adds the reservation the pull stories (US-52.44, US-52.46) consume.

acceptance_criteria.description: A move by the item's current holder (a new move_id, or the move_id of a move already requested on it) carrying a checkpoint_id of its own at the current epoch commits in one transaction, story FOR UPDATE then stage row FOR UPDATE: story_stages.pending_move set to {move_id, target, state: released, checkpoint_id, from_holder_id, released_at}, the claim released over the new edge :moved (claim_epoch + 1, assigned_holder_id nil, an in-flight row to queued with branch and pr_number kept, attempts not counted, never escalated), and a moved event with actor and reason; it answers 200 {move_id, state: released}.

A move by any other caller while a holder holds the item with a live lease sets pending_move with state requested and release_deadline_at = now + MOVE_RELEASE_SECONDS (default 600), inserts a thread message on the item ('Move to <target> requested by <actor>: checkpoint with work_item_checkpoint and call work_item_move with move_id <id>.'), appends a move_requested event, leaves the claim untouched and answers 202 {move_id, state: requested}.

A move of an item no holder holds sets pending_move released at once with checkpoint_id = the item's newest unfenced checkpoint (nil when none) and answers 200; a checkpoint_id that is not the caller's at the current epoch is refused 422 code checkpoint_not_current.

Loopctl.Workers.MoveDeadlineWorker (cron every minute) releases each requested move whose release_deadline_at has passed or whose holder's lease has lapsed, at that holder's newest unfenced checkpoint, with event reason holder_did_not_release; and clears each released move not pulled by released_at + MOVE_PULL_SECONDS (default 1800), with a move_expired event, leaving the item at queued for the loop.

While pending_move names a target other than loop, Progress.claim_story/3 refuses every caller that is not the target {:error, {:reserved_for_move, move_id, target}}, rendered 409 code reserved_for_move, and the implement candidate query skips the item (new Candidates predicate :not_move_reserved in implement@1); the target's claim clears pending_move and appends a move_pulled event in the claiming transaction.

A repeated move with the same move_id and target answers the first move's result and writes nothing; a different move_id while one is pending is refused 409 code move_pending naming the pending move_id and target; of two concurrent different moves on one item exactly one commits.

A move is refused before any write with 422 unknown_host (no unrevoked runner of the tenant has that name), 422 unknown_holder or 409 holder_ended (target holder), 422 target_unavailable (kind cloud: no cloud holder exists), 409 item_closed (stage done or failed), 409 item_escalated (stage escalated; re-queue it instead) or 422 already_held_by_target.

POST /api/v1/stories/:id/move (role: :agent) with {move_id, target: {kind: host | holder | loop | cloud, host, holder_id}, reason, checkpoint_id} and the MCP tool work_item_move reach Moves.move/4, the tool description naming every refusal and the 202 path, with a README row and a wiring test; MOVE_RELEASE_SECONDS and MOVE_PULL_SECONDS have rows in deploy/FLY_SECRETS.md.

test_cases.name: the holder moves its own item at implementing (DataCase)
preconditions: story placed on runner minis (fixture(:runner)) and advanced to implementing with branch and pr_number recorded; its runner_session holder H (US-52.15) with checkpoint C at the current epoch; DISPATCH_MAX_ATTEMPTS unset, so a counted release would escalate
steps: Moves.move(tenant.id, story.id, h_caller, %{move_id: m, target: %{kind: "host", host: "x1"}, checkpoint_id: c.id, reason: "rebalance"})
expected_results: stage queued, branch and pr_number kept, attempts unchanged, not escalated; claim_epoch + 1; assigned_holder_id nil; pending_move.state released with checkpoint_id c; one moved event

test_cases.name: a requested move, then the holder answers it (DataCase)
preconditions: story held by H; an orchestrator caller
steps: Moves.move as the orchestrator to host x1
H checkpoints and calls Moves.move with the same move_id
expected_results: first: 202 shape, claim unchanged, one thread message with the fixed text, release_deadline_at = now + 600 s; second: released as in TC-52.43.1

test_cases.name: an unheld item and a foreign checkpoint (DataCase)
preconditions: queued story with an unfenced checkpoint from an earlier holder; a second story held by H with a checkpoint by another holder
steps: move the queued story to loop
H moves the second story naming the other holder's checkpoint
expected_results: released with the earlier checkpoint id; {:error, :checkpoint_not_current}

test_cases.name: the deadline worker forces a release and expires an unpulled move (DataCase)
preconditions: a requested move with release_deadline_at in the past and H's checkpoint C; a released move with released_at 31 minutes ago
expected_results: first move released at C with reason holder_did_not_release; second pending_move nil and a move_expired event; the second run writes nothing

test_cases.name: only the target claims a reserved item; the driver skips it (DataCase)
preconditions: released move to holder T; holders T and U
expected_results: {:error, {:reserved_for_move, m, target}}; the story absent; T's claim succeeds, pending_move nil, one move_pulled event

test_cases.name: idempotent repeat and two racing moves (DataCase, committed, ProductionTopology)
preconditions: story held by H; async: false with the reason in the moduledoc (committed transactions racing)
steps: repeat a released move with the same move_id
Task.async two moves with different move_ids from two orchestrator callers
expected_results: same body, no new event; one {:ok, _} and one {:error, {:move_pending, winner_id, _}}

test_cases.name: every refusal, and a tenant-B runner name (ConnCase)
preconditions: a revoked runner named old; a runner named b1 in tenant B; an ended holder; stories at done, escalated and held by T
steps: POST move with host old, host b1, holder ended, kind cloud, the done story, the escalated story, holder T on T's story
expected_results: 422 unknown_host twice (tenant isolation); 409 holder_ended; 422 target_unavailable; 409 item_closed; 409 item_escalated; 422 already_held_by_target

test_cases.name: route gate and tool wiring (ConnCase + node --test)
preconditions: holder credential, user key, orchestrator key
expected_results: all three pass the role gate; the tool posts move_id, target and reason

technical_notes: Refactored, not added beside: the release is Stages.follow_release/5 (stages.ex:1731) with a new edge :moved and a new cause :moved in @release_causes (:179) that neither counts nor escalates; StageMachine gains {from, :queued, :moved} for @in_flight (stage_machine.ex:172,201) and clears/3 maps :moved to @released_clears (:522, :938), so branch and pr_number stay as on any release. The claim side is Progress' release path (claim_release_change/1, progress.ex:2041; unclaim_story/3 at :1593 is the model), clearing assigned_holder_id as US-52.14 AC-52.14.1 makes every release do.

pending_move is a jsonb column on story_stages beside merge_instruction and runner_absence (lib/loopctl/delivery/story_stage.ex:77-78): a reservation is current state of the item's stage row, locked with it (stages.ex:78-84), so a move and a resolve are serialized there as PRD section 7 point 3 requires. A separate table would need its own lock order.

Who may move: role: :agent (hierarchy), so a holder credential, a coordinating session's orchestrator key and fleet_dash's user key all pass (PRD R4 intervention verbs). Boundary moves into or out of an interactive session are refused here by US-52.45, which this story leaves room for: Moves.move/4 calls a boundary check that answers :ok until US-52.45.

Target resolution: host = an unrevoked runners row of the tenant whose name matches (Runners.list_runners/2, lib/loopctl/runners.ex:336; the join checks the machine name against it, runner_channel.ex:714); a runner session placed there is a holder with host = that name (US-52.15 AC-52.15.1), which is how AC-52.43.5 matches a host target. holder = a live Loopctl.Holders row (US-52.13).

Candidate skip: Loopctl.Agents.Candidates predicates (lib/loopctl/agents/candidates.ex:101,132,365) and implement@1's list (Loopctl.Agents.Specs.ImplementV1, read by DispatchDriver.candidates/1, dispatch_driver.ex:135); Loopctl.Agents.Spec validation (spec.ex) admits the new atom.

The thread message: Loopctl.Coordination.Messages.insert/2 with story_id (US-52.22). A runner session also gets a socket push from US-52.44, because its session may not read its inbox before the deadline.
Events: moved, move_requested, move_pulled, move_expired through release 3's log writer (README names table: work-item event log), each with actor and reason.
non_goals: Placing a host-targeted item and the runner's side of a move: US-52.44.
The interactive boundary (grant or user key): US-52.45.
Moving an escalated item: release 5's re-queue verb owns it.

failure_modes.partition: AC-52.43.4: a holder cut off from loopctl cannot answer a requested move; at its deadline or lease lapse the worker releases at its last checkpoint, and its later writes are fenced by the bumped epoch (US-52.42).
failure_modes.state: AC-52.43.1: the reservation lives on story_stages.pending_move and the shipped state in story_checkpoints, both in loopctl's Postgres; no machine holds the move.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.43.6: a retried move with the same move_id answers the first result; a second, different move is refused, never applied on top.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.43.4: a slow or silent holder delays a move by at most MOVE_RELEASE_SECONDS, and an unpulled move frees the item after MOVE_PULL_SECONDS.
failure_modes.reach: AC-52.43.2: the holder is reached through its item's thread, wherever it runs; the item is reached by id, never by machine.

defaults: MOVE_RELEASE_SECONDS = 600: how long a holder has to checkpoint and release a requested move.
MOVE_PULL_SECONDS = 1800: how long a released move waits for its target before the loop may take the item.
Thread message text as in AC-52.43.2.
definition_of_done: On a sandbox item held by a runner session: work_item_move to loop from another session returns 202, the item's thread shows the request, and after the holder answers SELECT pending_move->>'state' FROM story_stages WHERE story_id = <id> returns released.
